text: 🇲🇽⚖️ "From 2028, whoever wants to run for governor, head of government, or President of the Republic can only be Mexican." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 7, 2026 Sheinbaum signed the decree for the constitutional reform, which passed with two-thirds of both chambers of Congress and 22 state legislatures. It was published today in the official gazette. Candidates for President, governor or Mexico City head of government who hold another nationality must renounce it before registering with the electoral institute. Legal Counsel Luisa María Alcalde said regulations will set out the procedure, including with the other country. The government's weekly "lie detector" rejected claims that the reform strips political rights: anyone with dual nationality can still run once they renounce it.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>The US Cut a Fifth of Mexico's Gas Imports. The Country Had Three Days of Reserves.</u>

Cuitláhuac García, director of Mexico's National Gas Control Center (Cenagas), revealed that a week ago the United States warned it would stop sending "about a fifth of the imported natural gas" that flows through Mexico's pipelines. If imports from the US were cut entirely, Mexico would have gas for only three days, because the country has almost no storage. About 75% of the gas Mexico burns comes from the US, and it generates around 60% of the country's electricity. Neoliberal governments dismantled national production and never built storage, leaving that dependence in place. (El Financiero)
banner: US CUTS 20% OF GAS: 3 DAYS OF RESERVES

🔥🇲🇽 <u>PAN Ex-Deputy Sentenced for 65 Million Peso Fraud, and Maru Campos's Government Kept Paying Him</u>

A court in Tlalnepantla sentenced Ismael Mario Rodríguez Saldaña, a former PAN state deputy in Chihuahua and a construction businessman, to two years in prison and ordered him to repay 65 million pesos for defrauding the developer Roagmex. Companies tied to him and his family had received at least four public-works contracts worth 196.27 million pesos from the Chihuahua Ministry of Communications and Public Works under PAN Governor Maru Campos. This is the same governor who lectures the federal government about the rule of law.

🇲🇽🩺 <u>After Newborn Deaths in Jalisco, IMSS Opens an Independent Audit and Inspects All 77 Neonatal ICUs</u>

Mexico's IMSS has opened an independent clinical audit into infections and deaths in the neonatal ICU of the National Medical Center in Jalisco, its second largest. A panel of neonatologists, infectious disease specialists and epidemiologists will review every file, and IMSS cannot change their conclusions. The national epidemiology lab, InDRE, will trace every microorganism found. Health authorities are also inspecting all 77 IMSS neonatal ICUs and their 660 cribs nationwide, checking hand-washing, catheter care, antibiotic use, water and staffing. IMSS director Zoé Robledo said the goal is to find failures and prevent new cases, not to criminalize medical staff.
banner: IMSS: AUDIT OF ALL 77 NEWBORN ICUS

🔥🇲🇽 <u>A Supreme Court Justice Wrote a Ruling for a Coca-Cola Bottler, Then Pulled It</u>

Before today's Supreme Court debate on banning junk food in Mexican schools, Justice Giovanni Figueroa Mejía circulated a draft that would have granted an amparo to Embotelladora Las Margaritas (Grupo Rica), which bottles Coca-Cola, Sprite, Fanta, Del Valle and Powerade. The draft let it sell its products in universities again, arguing that "the elimination of foods that do not favor students' health" applies "only to schools that provide basic education." Contralínea obtained that first version. Figueroa swapped it for a draft that upholds the SEP ban before the vote. The original stayed on record.
banner: JUNK FOOD: JUSTICE'S COKE DRAFT PULLED

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Mexico Gave Away More in Tax Breaks Than It Spent Building Infrastructure</u>

According to Oxfam México, tax exemptions, credits and reduced rates cost Mexico's treasury 1.58 trillion pesos in 2025, or 4.4% of GDP. That's more than the federal government spent on physical investment that year. Most of these breaks go to the highest-income households and large corporations, and they get far less oversight than ordinary spending: almost nothing is published about who receives them or what they produce. These privileges were written in during the neoliberal decades, and they are why Hacienda now lists closing loopholes and fighting evasion as its main ways to raise revenue.
banner: TAX BREAKS: 4.4% OF GDP, MOSTLY THE RICH

text:
🇲🇽⚡ <u>Sheinbaum Lays Out a 1.16 Trillion Peso Plan to Rebuild Mexico's Power Grid</u>

President Sheinbaum announced the largest electricity and gas investment in Mexico's history: 1.16 trillion pesos this term, not counting oil, fertilizers or petrochemicals. Of that, 794 billion pesos goes to generation, 161 billion to transmission, about 72 billion to distribution and 140.9 billion to gas pipelines, adding roughly 38,000 megawatts. Part of it comes from mixed projects with private financing, but the infrastructure stays with CFE. The utility the neoliberals wanted to sell off for scrap now has, in Sheinbaum's words, "perfect" finances and will close 2026 with a surplus.

🇲🇽📈 <u>World Bank Raises Mexico's Growth Forecast for 2026 and 2027</u>

The World Bank now expects Mexico's economy to grow 1.4% in 2026 and 1.8% in 2027, up from the 1.3% and 1.7% it projected in June, and to reach 2.2% in 2028, El Economista reports. The bank says tight monetary policy needed to bring inflation down and smaller public-investment momentum are holding the big Latin American economies back. On trade, it found that "export volumes show remarkable resilience" despite the tariff swings coming out of Washington.
banner: WORLD BANK: MEXICO GDP UP TO 1.4%

🇲🇽🚗 <u>Mexico's Homegrown EV Olinia Gets Its Own National Lottery Ticket</u>

Mexico's Lotería Nacional unveiled Special Draw No. 317, dedicated to Olinia, the government's project to build the country's first national maker of small, affordable electric vehicles. More than 70 Mexican scientists and engineers work on it, and its assembly center is in Puebla. The draw is October 16, with a 27-million-peso top prize. "Olinia is starting to stop being a project and to become an idea that many Mexicans recognize as their own," said project director Roberto Capuano, as Olinia enters its second stage: becoming a company.
banner: OLINIA EV GETS ITS OWN LOTTERY TICKET

🇲🇽🌱 <u>Mexico City Avoided a Million Tonnes of Emissions in One Year</u>

Opening Mexico City's Climate and Nature Action Week, Mayor Clara Brugada said her government avoided more than one million tonnes of greenhouse gases in the past year, twice Cabo Verde's annual emissions. Eco-technologies are now installed in 19,000 homes, with a target of 50,000, and recycling rose 45% in seven months. "There is no climate justice without social justice, nor social justice without gender justice," Brugada said. Her government is studying how to speed up the switch away from fossil fuels for power generation.
